gap: No result ChatGPT got states how many days each wireless pick lasts between charges at 3 hours of gaming a day on its low-latency 2.4 GHz dongle, or its cost per rated battery hour. Here are both: the Arctis Nova 5X gets about 14 days (42 h ÷ 3) at $3.07/h, the HyperX Cloud III S Wireless about 40 days (120 h ÷ 3) at $1.08/h, and the Logitech G Pro X 2 about 17 days (50 h ÷ 3) at $4.40/h. ChatGPT's '60 hours' for the Nova 5X is not its 2.4 GHz gaming figure.
standout_why: Compared against SoundGuys (cited by ChatGPT in both chats). It gives the raw inputs: Nova 5X 'over 42 hrs (2.4GHz)' and Cloud III S Wireless 'up to 120 hrs (2.4GHz) / 200 hrs (Bluetooth)'. It does not work out days between charges or cost per battery hour, and it does not point out that ChatGPT's cited '60 hours' is not the dongle figure. The fetched page has no G Pro X 2 or EKSA figures. GamesRadar (cited), Tom's Guide and the RTINGS gaming list came back as page titles only. That means I could not confirm they lack these numbers, and the score is held at 1 because the cited rival already has the inputs.
decides: For an Xbox + PC buyer it confirms the Nova 5X, because SoundGuys lists Xbox only for the Nova 5X among these wireless picks. It also corrects the expectation to about two weeks between charges at 3 h/day, not the roughly 20 days that 60 h ÷ 3 implies. For PC/PS5/Switch buyers (no Xbox) it moves the pick to the HyperX Cloud III S Wireless. It is at the same price ($129.99 at HyperX vs $129.00 for the Nova 5X on Amazon) with about 2.9× the rated 2.4 GHz runtime (120 ÷ 42), and it costs much less than the G Pro X 2 per battery hour. The wired HyperX Cloud III ($57.99) needs no charging and is the only candidate whose maker lists PC, PS5, Xbox Series X|S and Switch.
